phase3_findings.description: No test sends a failing slash command through the typed input path: handleUserInput passes { typed: true } to runCommandInput at line 249, but the controller tests call runCommandInput directly and the widget's failed-turn tests send only plain text, so dropping the flag would stop refilling a failed typed command with every test still passing.

The guard that keeps a saved conversation ID another tab or widget stored while a failed restore was pending is untested: no test changes the stored conversation value during a pending restore and then lets the restore fail.

Probably only one side of the react-chatbot-kit default-import unwrap (chatbotKit.Chatbot ?? chatbotKit) runs under vitest, and no ESM smoke test imports the built package, so reverting the unwrap could break Node-ESM consumers with tests green; part of the deferred out-of-scope bundle.

Two blockGuards.ts docstrings overstate: line 1 says these are shape checks BlockRenderer uses, but isMalformedBlock and isBuiltInType are used only by ChatWidget.appendBlocks; line 10 says customRendererFor never returns an Object.prototype name, but the hasOwnProperty check only excludes inherited members, so an own toString or constructor function is still returned.

Several added ChatWidget.tsx comments (615-620 CSS sizing, 53-57 CommonJS interop, 239-242 and 253-256 mobile viewport history) mostly explain background rather than naming the change a maintainer must not make; all are factually accurate.

A host block renderer that throws while it is called escapes the per-block error boundary: renderBlock(block) runs inside BlockRenderer's own render (children expression at line 113), so custom(block) at 107 runs before BlockErrorBoundary exists, nothing above catches it (chatConfig.tsx 102-108, react-chatbot-kit), and React unmounts the whole widget. The pre-existing file header (5-7) claims one malformed block cannot break the widget; the existing test covers only a renderer that returns a later-throwing component. Pre-existing, but appendBlocks now routes host-shaped data to host renderers after mount.

customRendererFor returns undefined for an own blockRenderers entry that is not a function, so such a block renders nothing with no log; for appendBlocks the warning at ChatWidget.tsx 538 says no blockRenderers entry exists when one does, pointing the host at the wrong cause.

The try block guarding host.onTurnFailed also wraps the attachmentListeners notification (line 423): a throwing listener is logged as 'onTurnFailed failed' and later listeners are never told the attachments were restored, so chips can fall out of sync; the only current listener cannot throw.

The two mount() diagnostics ('The widget was unmounted; ignoring the call.' at line 40 and 'The widget did not render; dropping N queued call(s).' at line 54) do not name which handle method was ignored or dropped.

The failed-turn refill (onTurnFailed, the typed option, re-staging attachments, ChatWidget.tsx 349-355, README 120 and its tests) is a second concern bundled into this PR against CONTRIBUTING.md line 20 ('One concern per pull request'); nothing in appendBlocks depends on it and the PR description does not mention it. The description also omits that a blocks: [] answer with no sources now ends the turn silently instead of apologising (ChatController.ts 398-403, types.ts 110-115). The deferred iteration-2 scope finding listed only the viewport, CSS, interop and viewport-test changes, so this is new evidence.

The blockGuards.ts module header says it holds shape checks BlockRenderer uses to pick a renderer, which is false for isMalformedBlock (24-31) and isBuiltInType (33): BlockRenderer imports only customRendererFor, isChartBlock, isTableBlock and isTextBlock.

report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no Critical findings; two Important findings and ten Suggestions sit below the critical threshold; four checklist items are inconclusive)

The PR can merge: no finding or checklist failure reaches the critical threshold, and the `appendBlocks` buffering, live routing, restore handling and `mount()` replay all checked out.

Rule applied: rule 6 — only findings and checklist results below the threshold, and inconclusive items, remain → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟠 Important / Major

1. The PR bundles a second feature, the failed-turn refill, against CONTRIBUTING.md line 20 ("One concern per pull request"). The feature puts a failed typed message back in the composer and stages its attachments again, in `src/chat/ChatController.ts` (lines 77-82, 249-286, 350-356 and 417-428), `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 349-355, README line 120 and its tests. Nothing in `appendBlocks` depends on it, and the PR description does not mention it. The PR description also leaves out a data-source contract change: a `blocks: []` answer with no sources now ends the turn silently instead of showing the apology (ChatController.ts lines 398-403, types.ts lines 110-115). The iteration-2 scope finding was deferred, but it named only the viewport and CSS changes, so this is new evidence. (raised by 2/5 agents; the second agent's finding shares the file, kind and line range by signature but describes a different defect, item 1 under Suggestion)
2. A host block renderer that throws while it is called escapes the per-block error boundary and unmounts the whole widget, in `src/blocks/BlockRenderer.tsx` lines 106-113. `renderBlock(block)` runs inside `BlockRenderer`'s own render, so `custom(block)` runs before `BlockErrorBoundary` exists, and no boundary sits above it. The file header (lines 5-7, not changed by this diff) says one malformed block cannot break the widget. The existing test covers only a renderer that returns a component that throws later. This is older than the PR, but `appendBlocks` now sends host-shaped data to host renderers after mount. (raised by 1/5 agents)

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. The `onTurnFailed` try block in `src/chat/ChatController.ts` lines 418-427 also wraps the attachment-listener calls. A listener that throws is logged as "onTurnFailed failed", and the listeners after it are not told about the restored attachments. Today's only listener cannot throw. (raised by 2/5 agents; signature-matched with Important item 1, which describes a different defect)
2. No test sends a failing slash command through the typed input path, so dropping `{ typed: true }` at `src/chat/ChatController.ts` line 249 would leave every test green. (raised by 1/5 agents)
3. No test covers the guard in `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 424-431 that keeps a saved conversation ID another tab stored while a failed restore was pending. (raised by 1/5 agents)
4. Probably only one side of the react-chatbot-kit default-import unwrap in `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` lines 53-58 runs under the tests, and no ESM smoke test imports the built package. This is part of the deferred out-of-scope bundle. (raised by 1/5 agents)
5. Two docstrings in `src/blocks/blockGuards.ts` overstate. Line 1 says the module holds shape checks BlockRenderer uses, but `isMalformedBlock` and `isBuiltInType` are used only by `ChatWidget.appendBlocks`. Line 10 says "never an Object.prototype name", but the `hasOwnProperty` check only excludes inherited names, so an own `toString` function is still returned. (raised by 1/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: making the sentences true changes no output or branch of customRendererFor, isMalformedBlock or isBuiltInType; git grep —no-index of view-head for both phrases found only blockGuards.ts lines 1 and 10; blockGuards is imported only by BlockRenderer.tsx and ChatWidget.tsx and is not re-exported -->
6. The module header of `src/blocks/blockGuards.ts` line 1 says BlockRenderer uses these checks, which is false for `isMalformedBlock` and `isBuiltInType`. (raised by 1/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: same as item 5 — no output changes, no reader of the phrase outside the file, internal module -->
7. Several added comments in `src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx` (lines 615-620, 53-57, 239-242 and 253-256) explain CSS or mobile-viewport background rather than just the change a maintainer must not make. All four are accurate. (raised by 1/5 agents)
8. `customRendererFor` in `src/blocks/blockGuards.ts` lines 15-17 returns nothing for a `blockRenderers` entry that is not a function, so such a block renders nothing with no log. For `appendBlocks`, the warning at ChatWidget.tsx line 538 says no entry exists when one does. (raised by 1/5 agents)
9. The two `mount()` warnings in `src/mount.tsx` lines 40 and 54 do not name the handle method that was ignored or dropped. (raised by 1/5 agents)
- VC-35: FAIL (suggestion) — The comment asserts that once the widget unmounts, a handle kept past that point does nothing. [src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:506]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment at ChatWidget.tsx:506 says a handle kept past unmount 'does nothing'. Only appendBlocks (517-520) checks aliveRef. The other handle methods (useImperativeHandle 566-578) have no such guard. setLayout is changeLayout (190-195), which calls storage.set('layout', mode) after unmount. open() and close() go through setOpen (170-183), which calls storage.set('open', ...) when initialOpen==='remember'. newConversation calls controller.newConversation() on the disposed widget's controller. So a kept handle still does persistent work (storage writes) after unmount, and the absolute wording is wrong. I did not read the storage implementation. The counterexample is the unguarded setLayout, which reaches storage.set. This is a comment inaccuracy only, and the behavior is mostly harmless.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (4)

<details><summary>4 items</summary>

- VC-7: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The ControllerHost.onTurnFailed TSDoc says `text` is what the user typed. handleUserInput passes text.trim() into runCommandInput for slash commands, and the untrimmed text into sendTurn otherwise, so onTurnFailed receives the trimmed input for a typed slash command. [src/chat/ChatController.ts:78]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Trace confirmed: ChatController.ts:248-249 calls runCommandInput(text.trim(), {typed:true}) for slash input and :252 calls sendTurn(text, {typed:true}) untrimmed otherwise. runCommandInput passes `input` (trimmed) to sendTurn (:262,272,286), performTurn calls host.onTurnFailed?.(text) at :419. So '  /report weekly ' yields onTurnFailed('/report weekly'); the TSDoc at :78 says 'text is what they typed', which differs only by leading/trailing whitespace. ChatWidget.tsx:349-354 writes the received text into the composer. The factual behaviour matches the claim, but no requirement from an unchanged file (outside ChatController.ts) was found that demands the exact untrimmed text, and the discrepancy is whitespace-only, so I cannot show a broken requirement (FAIL) nor rule out one (INVALID).

  </details>

- VC-20: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts that emulated mobile viewports never fire a second resize event after the window's resize event when they settle to their final size. [src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:242]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  The comment at src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:239-242 claims emulated mobile viewports never fire a second resize event. That is a claim about DevTools/browser behavior, and no repository source or dependency source settles it. I read the code (243-259). It behaves correctly with either outcome. The window 'resize' and visualViewport 'resize' listeners both call keepInsideViewport, and an effect re-clamps on open (257-259). I could not run a browser to check the emulation behavior, so the 'never' wording is unverified. Missing evidence: a run of a DevTools device-emulation toggle logging resize events.

  </details>

- VC-26: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — By the time ChatWidget's no-deps layout effect sets `mountedResetKeyRef.current = chatResetKey` for a newly keyed Chatbot, the controller is already bound to that Chatbot's state, so an append routed to `controller.addMessages` because the keys match reaches the new transcript rather than the unmounted one. [src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:546]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Read src/chat/ChatController.ts:494-499: the adapter ActionProvider binds the controller to the kit's setState inside its constructor (controller.bind(setState) when setState is a function). ChatWidget.tsx:498-501 sets mountedResetKeyRef in a no-deps layout effect, and :549 routes on it. Whether the controller is already bound to the new Chatbot's state by then depends on when react-chatbot-kit constructs the ActionProvider (during render, a ref/memo initializer, or an effect). No dependency_sources were supplied and the library is not in the views, so I could not read that. The library does exist in the working tree's node_modules (react-chatbot-kit/src/components/Chatbot/Chatbot.tsx), but I did not rely on it, since the rules bar falling back to the working tree. Missing evidence: the Chatbot.tsx instantiation site of ActionProvider and its timing relative to layout effects.

  </details>

- VC-31: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts that a turn, command, new conversation or History switch made since the restore started wins over that restore. [src/widget/ChatWidget.tsx:388]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  ChatWidget.tsx:384-394 snapshots controller.activity and requestedResetKeyRef and skips the restore if either changed. Turns (ChatController.handleUserInput:244), commands (runCommandInput:257), new conversation (onNewConversation -> remountChat, ChatWidget.tsx:330-333) and a successful History switch (remountChat at :402) all change one of them, so the comment holds for those. Counterexample: a History switch whose getConversation rejects while the restore is pending. loadConversation returns false at :404-406 without remountChat, and switchToConversation (:441-444) calls controller.reply, which only calls addMessages (ChatController.ts:313-315) and does not bump activity or the reset key. The restore then resolves, passes the guard, calls switchConversation(saved) and remountChat. That replaces the error reply and moves the user to the saved conversation. A failed switch arguably was never 'made', so the comment may be literally accurate. I found no unchanged requirement file (no .src instruction files in the head view) showing that a failed switch must win, so I cannot grade FAIL or INVALID.

  </details>

</details>

Whether the controller is already bound to the new Chatbot's state by then depends on when react-chatbot-kit constructs the ActionProvider (during render, a ref/memo initializer, or an effect). No dependency_sources were supplied and the library is not in the views, so I could not read that. The library does exist in the working tree's node_modules (react-chatbot-kit/src/components/Chatbot/Chatbot.tsx), but I did not rely on it, since the rules bar falling back to the working tree. Missing evidence: the Chatbot.tsx instantiation site of ActionProvider and its timing relative to layout effects.

checklist.claim: The comment asserts that a turn, command, new conversation or History switch made since the restore started wins over that restore.
checklist.source_excerpt: // A turn, command, new conversation or History switch since the restore started wins.
checklist.verify_against: `loadConversation` and `switchToConversation` in ChatWidget.tsx and `ChatController.reply` in src/chat/ChatController.ts
checklist.verify_hint: Trace a History switch whose `getConversation` rejects while the restore is still pending: `switchToConversation` then calls `controller.reply` without `remountChat`, so check whether `controller.activity` or `requestedResetKeyRef` changes before the restore resolves
checklist.evidence: ChatWidget.tsx:384-394 snapshots controller.activity and requestedResetKeyRef and skips the restore if either changed. Turns (ChatController.handleUserInput:244), commands (runCommandInput:257), new conversation (onNewConversation -> remountChat, ChatWidget.tsx:330-333) and a successful History switch (remountChat at :402) all change one of them, so the comment holds for those. Counterexample: a History switch whose getConversation rejects while the restore is pending. loadConversation returns false at :404-406 without remountChat, and switchToConversation (:441-444) calls controller.reply, which only calls addMessages (ChatController.ts:313-315) and does not bump activity or the reset key. The restore then resolves, passes the guard, calls switchConversation(saved) and remountChat. That replaces the error reply and moves the user to the saved conversation. A failed switch arguably was never 'made', so the comment may be literally accurate. I found no unchanged requirement file (no .src instruction files in the head view) showing that a failed switch must win, so I cannot grade FAIL or INVALID.

checklist.claim: The comment asserts that once the widget unmounts, a handle kept past that point does nothing.
checklist.source_excerpt: // False once the widget unmounts; a handle kept past that point does nothing.
checklist.verify_against: The handle built by `useImperativeHandle` at ChatWidget.tsx 566-578 and `setOpen`/`changeLayout` at 170-197
checklist.verify_hint: Trace calls on a kept handle after unmount other than appendBlocks: `open()` or `close()` with `initialOpen='remember'` (storage.set('open')), `setLayout()` (storage.set('layout')), and `newConversation()` on the disposed controller
checklist.evidence: The comment at ChatWidget.tsx:506 says a handle kept past unmount 'does nothing'. Only appendBlocks (517-520) checks aliveRef. The other handle methods (useImperativeHandle 566-578) have no such guard. setLayout is changeLayout (190-195), which calls storage.set('layout', mode) after unmount. open() and close() go through setOpen (170-183), which calls storage.set('open', ...) when initialOpen==='remember'. newConversation calls controller.newConversation() on the disposed widget's controller. So a kept handle still does persistent work (storage writes) after unmount, and the absolute wording is wrong. I did not read the storage implementation. The counterexample is the unguarded setLayout, which reaches storage.set. This is a comment inaccuracy only, and the behavior is mostly harmless.
